name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent David Taylor running with a large fundraising edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price near-certain R win
Democratic challenger has minimal reported fundraising
model.rationale: The R+21 district lean, Taylor's incumbency and roughly $1.1 million raised against a challenger with no reported finances, and Polymarket pricing the Republican at 98% all point the same direction. Nothing in the evidence supports moving materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Taylor would be the main way this moves.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-02 is a heavily Republican southern Ohio seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. Incumbent David Taylor is running for reelection after clearing his primary, and he holds a clear financial advantage, having raised about $1.1 million with $443,000 on hand. Democrat Jennifer Mazzuckelli has no reported fundraising totals.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Taylor roughly a 98% chance of winning. With the district lean, incumbency, and money all aligned, the race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being ordinary first-term incumbent variance rather than any specific competitive signal.
